prompt: What is the stereochemical outcome of acid-catalyzed addition of H2O to 1-butene in the laboratory?

choices.text: A racemic mixture of (R)- and (S)-2-butanol
Only (R)-2-butanol, a single enantiomer
choices.why: Nothing in the reaction favors one enantiomer, so both form.

choices.text: Only (S)-2-butanol, a single enantiomer
choices.why: Nothing in the reaction favors one enantiomer, so both form.

choices.text: (R)- and (S)-2-butanol in unequal amounts
choices.why: The two enantiomers form through mirror-image transition states of identical energy, so their amounts are equal.

explanation: 1-Butene is achiral, and the 2-butanol produced is a racemic mixture of R and S enantiomers: 50% of each.

prompt: What percentage of the 2-butanol from acid-catalyzed hydration of 1-butene is the (R) enantiomer?
explanation: The product is racemic: 50% (R)-2-butanol and 50% (S)-2-butanol, because the planar carbocation reacts equally well from the top and the bottom.

prompt: Why is the carbocation formed by protonating 1-butene achiral?

choices.text: Its trivalent carbon is sp2 and planar, giving the cation a plane of symmetry
It is a primary carbocation, so no carbon in it has four different groups
choices.why: Protonating 1-butene gives a secondary carbocation. It is achiral because it is planar.

choices.text: Its positive carbon is sp3-hybridized and carries a lone pair of electrons
choices.why: The trivalent carbon is sp2 and planar, with no lone pair.

choices.text: Water is already bonded to the positive carbon when it forms
choices.why: Water reacts with the carbocation afterward; the cation itself is achiral because it is planar.

explanation: Protonation of 1-butene gives a secondary carbocation. Its trivalent carbon is sp2-hybridized and planar, so the cation has a plane of symmetry and is achiral. Water can react with it equally well from the top or the bottom.

prompt: Why does water attack the sec-butyl carbocation equally often from its top and bottom faces?

choices.text: The two transition states are mirror images, so their energies and rates are identical
The two transition states are diastereomers that happen to have similar energies
choices.why: They are mirror images, so their energies are identical, not just similar.

choices.text: Each water molecule bonds to the top and bottom faces at the same time
choices.why: Each water molecule attacks one face; the two pathways are separate but equally likely.

choices.text: The carbocation switches rapidly back and forth between two chiral forms
choices.why: The carbocation is planar and achiral; no switching is involved.

explanation: Reaction from the top leads to (S)-2-butanol through TS 1, and from the bottom to (R)-2-butanol through TS 2. The two transition states are mirror images, so they have identical energies, form at identical rates, and are equally likely (Figure 8.12.1).

prompt: What is the general rule when achiral reactants form a new chirality center?

choices.text: The product is always a racemic mixture of enantiomers
The product is always a single enantiomer
choices.why: Optical activity can't appear from nowhere; achiral reactants give a racemic mixture.

choices.text: The product is a mixture of diastereomers in unequal amounts
choices.why: With achiral reactants, the new center forms as two enantiomers in exactly equal amounts.

choices.text: The product is optically active if the reaction is fast enough
choices.why: Speed doesn't matter. An optically active product needs an optically active reactant or a chiral environment.

explanation: As a general rule, the formation of a new chirality center by achiral reactants always leads to a racemic mixture of enantiomeric products. Optical activity can't appear from nowhere.

prompt: Under what conditions can an optically active product form in a reaction?

choices.text: Only from an optically active reactant or in a chiral environment
Whenever a new chirality center is formed in the reaction
choices.why: If the reactants are achiral, a new chirality center forms as a racemic mixture.

choices.text: Whenever the reaction goes through a carbocation intermediate
choices.why: A planar, achiral carbocation gives a racemic product.

choices.text: Whenever a strong acid is used to catalyze the reaction
choices.why: Acid catalysis gave racemic 2-butanol from 1-butene.

explanation: Optical activity can't appear from nowhere. An optically active product can only result by starting with an optically active reactant or in a chiral environment, such as an enzyme's active site.

prompt: What is the net optical rotation, in degrees, of the 2-butanol mixture made by acid-catalyzed hydration of 1-butene?
explanation: The product is a racemic mixture, with equal amounts of (R)- and (S)-2-butanol. The rotations of the two enantiomers cancel, so the mixture is optically inactive: 0°.

prompt: What forms when aconitase catalyzes the addition of water to cis-aconitate in the citric acid cycle?

A racemic mixture of isocitrate enantiomers

choices.text: Only the (2S,3R) enantiomer of isocitrate
choices.why: The enzyme gives the (2R,3S) enantiomer.

choices.text: Equal amounts of all four stereoisomers of isocitrate
choices.why: Enzyme-catalyzed reactions often give a single enantiomer; here only (2R,3S)-isocitrate forms.

explanation: Even though cis-aconitate is achiral, aconitase gives only (2R,3S)-isocitrate. Enzyme-catalyzed reactions often give a single enantiomer, even when the substrate is achiral.

prompt: Why does the aconitase-catalyzed hydration of cis-aconitate give a single enantiomer even though cis-aconitate is achiral?

choices.text: The enzyme holds the prochiral substrate in a chiral environment, so its faces differ
cis-Aconitate is itself a chiral molecule, so its two faces already differ
choices.why: cis-Aconitate is achiral but prochiral. The chirality comes from the enzyme.

choices.text: The reaction goes through a planar carbocation that water attacks from both faces
choices.why: That would give a racemic mixture, as with 1-butene in the lab.

choices.text: The enzyme destroys one enantiomer of a racemic product after it forms
choices.why: Only one enantiomer forms in the first place, because addition occurs on only one face.

explanation: cis-Aconitate is a prochiral molecule held in a chiral environment by aconitase. In this environment the two faces of the double bond are chemically distinct, and addition occurs only on the Re face at carbon 2.

prompt: On which face of cis-aconitate's double bond, at carbon 2, does aconitase add water?

choices.text: Only the Re face
Only the Si face
choices.why: The section says addition occurs only on the Re face at carbon 2.

choices.text: Both faces equally

choices.text: Whichever face the enzyme happens to meet first
choices.why: In the enzyme's chiral environment the faces are distinct, and addition is always on the Re face.

explanation: Held in the chiral environment of aconitase, the two faces of the double bond are chemically distinct, and addition occurs only on the Re face at carbon 2, giving (2R,3S)-isocitrate.

prompt: How many stereoisomers of isocitrate are produced when aconitase adds water to cis-aconitate?
explanation: Only one, the (2R,3S) enantiomer, forms. The enzyme's chiral environment makes the two faces of the double bond different, and water adds only on the Re face at carbon 2.

prompt: How do enzyme-catalyzed additions to achiral substrates often differ from comparable laboratory reactions?

choices.text: Enzymes often give a single enantiomer, while achiral lab reactions give a racemic mixture
Enzymes give racemic mixtures, while achiral lab reactions give a single enantiomer
choices.why: This is reversed.

choices.text: Enzymes always give achiral products, while lab reactions give chiral ones
choices.why: Aconitase gives a chiral product, (2R,3S)-isocitrate.

choices.text: Both always give racemic mixtures, since the substrates are achiral
choices.why: Enzymes provide a chiral environment and often give a single enantiomer.

explanation: In contrast to laboratory reactions, enzyme-catalyzed biological reactions often give a single enantiomer of a chiral product, even when the substrate is achiral, because the enzyme provides a chiral environment.

prompt: Which acid-catalyzed hydration creates a new chirality center and so gives a racemic mixture?

choices.text: 1-Butene, giving 2-butanol
Propene, giving 2-propanol
choices.why: In 2-propanol, the −OH carbon carries two identical CH3 groups, so it isn't a chirality center.

choices.text: 2-Methylpropene, giving 2-methyl-2-propanol
choices.why: The −OH carbon carries three identical CH3 groups; no chirality center forms.

choices.text: Ethylene, giving ethanol
choices.why: Ethanol has no chirality center.

explanation: In 2-butanol, carbon 2 carries H, OH, CH3 and CH2CH3, four different groups, so it is a chirality center. Because the reactants are achiral, the product is racemic. The other alcohols have no chirality center.

prompt: Acid-catalyzed hydration of 1-pentene, CH2=CHCH2CH2CH3, gives 2-pentanol. What is the stereochemistry of the product?

choices.text: A racemic, optically inactive mixture of (R)- and (S)-2-pentanol
Pure (R)-2-pentanol, a single optically active enantiomer
choices.why: Achiral reactants can't give a single enantiomer; the planar carbocation reacts equally from both faces.

choices.text: An optically active mixture that is richer in (S)-2-pentanol
choices.why: With achiral reactants both enantiomers form equally, so the mixture is optically inactive.

choices.text: No stereoisomers, because 2-pentanol has no chirality center
choices.why: Carbon 2 carries H, OH, CH3 and CH2CH2CH3, four different groups, so it is a chirality center.

explanation: Like 1-butene, 1-pentene is achiral and gives a planar secondary carbocation that water attacks equally from both faces. The new chirality center at carbon 2 forms as a racemic mixture.

prompt: What kind of carbocation forms when 1-butene is protonated during acid-catalyzed hydration?

choices.text: A secondary carbocation
A primary carbocation
choices.why: The proton adds to carbon 1, leaving the positive charge on carbon 2, which is bonded to two other carbons.

choices.text: A tertiary carbocation
choices.why: Carbon 2 of 1-butene is bonded to only two other carbons, so the cation is secondary.

choices.text: No carbocation; water adds in a single step
choices.why: 1-Butene is first protonated to give a carbocation intermediate.

explanation: 1-Butene is first protonated to yield an intermediate secondary carbocation. Its sp2, planar trivalent carbon gives it a plane of symmetry, so it is achiral.
